advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the AST/source-parsing guard in `test_review_bot_lifespan_marker_covers_autouse_setup` with a behavioral check (or drop it), as it couples to another test's decorator structure and cannot detect the runtime regression it targets.
evidence: tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:64-78 `_timeout_marker_seconds` does `module = ast.parse(path.read_text(...))` then matches `decorator.func.attr == "timeout"` on a function whose `node.name == test_name` — parsing source code under test as the assertion.
tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:132-138 keys on the literal test name `"test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs"` and asserts `seconds >= 30`.

The target `@pytest.mark.timeout(30)` (tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1758) is an int literal in an executable test file, not a non-executable instruction/config artifact, so the Rule-5 structural-boundary exception does not apply (unlike the sibling `_ini()` checks that parse pyproject.toml).

ABSENCE: the test exercises no runtime path — it does not construct the TestClient, run pytest-timeout, or reproduce the xdist worker-crash shape; it only compares one hardcoded number (30, duplicated across two files with no shared constant) against another. It survives no rename and catches no real regression.
advisory.finding: `test_review_bot_lifespan_marker_covers_autouse_setup` asserts on the AST/decorator structure of the source-under-test (`test_review_bot.py`) rather than any observable behavior: it statically re-reads the `@pytest.mark.timeout(...)` literal for a named function and asserts `>= 30`. It breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (renaming the target test, restructuring the marker) and cannot detect the runtime regression (tight budget → worker crash) it claims to guard.
scenarios: Someone renames `test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs` for clarity — this guard fails on `assert seconds is not None` with no behavior change.

The marker is refactored to a shared constant or module-level pytestmark — `decorator.args[0]` is no longer an `ast.Constant`, so `_timeout_marker_seconds` returns `None` and the guard fails spuriously.
